key_insight: UNITE enables truly end-to-end training by unifying the image tokenizer and latent diffusion generator into a single, weight‑shared generative encoder, removing the need for a separately trained frozen tokenizer and reducing representational mismatch.
problem_solved: State-of-the-art latent diffusion workflows require multi‑stage training (train tokenizer first, then freeze it and train diffusion), which is complex, brittle, and can cause suboptimal latent representations and artifacts when the tokenizer and diffusion model are not jointly optimized.
method: Design a Generative Encoder that simultaneously serves as an image tokenizer and latent generator through weight sharing between encoding and generative pathways.
Train the autoencoder and diffusion denoiser jointly end‑to‑end with combined reconstruction + denoising objectives, removing the frozen-tokenizer stage.
Optimize a unified latent space so the diffusion model learns directly on latents produced by the encoder, reducing representation mismatch and simplifying the pipeline.
impact: Simplifies LDM training pipelines, improves alignment between tokenizer and denoiser for better sample fidelity, and lowers development complexity and potential failure modes for practitioners building latent generative models.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: Generative Encoder with shared weights linking encoder (tokenizer) and latent generator, feeding the diffusion denoiser.
Pipeline comparison: staged (tokenizer → freeze → diffusion) vs UNITE end‑to‑end training (single flow) illustrated as side‑by‑side timelines.
Loss breakdown chart: reconstruction loss + denoising loss and how they jointly update shared weights.
Before/after examples: qualitative outputs showing reduced artifacts and improved fidelity when training end‑to‑end.
paper_title: End-to-End Training for Unified Tokenization and Latent Denoising
paper_authors: Shivam Duggal, Xingjian Bai, Zongze Wu, Richard Zhang, Eli Shechtman
